title: Config
description:
We need to make git store your information instead of default data, because git tracks who did what.
Git has global and repo scope config.

---
## Assignment:
Set your identity! Fist check if it's already set.
```bash
git config get user.name
git config get user.email
```
If they arn't, then set them using `config set`. Use the same email and username as your github account (if you don't have one, make one [here](https://github.com))
```bash
git config set --global user.name "github_username"
git config set --global user.email "email@example.com"
```
Finally, set a git default branch (later explained). Run:
```bash
git config set --global init.defaultBranch master
```
> Right now, we are using `master`, the git default, but in like 40-50 lessons, we are going to switch to `main` which is the git_hub_ default.

---
Check if it worked.
Your ~/.gitconfig stores your . . . git config. Read it
```bash
cat ~/.gitconfig
```
